title: Egg white‐derived preparations attenuate fatty acid‐induced lipid accumulation and alter lipid metabolism in HepG2 cells
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Obesity-related lipid metabolic disorders are often characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation, highlighting the need for safe dietary strategies. Egg white protein is a high-quality dietary protein with potential metabolic benefits. However, whether digestion and fermentation enhance its lipid-regulatory activity remains unclear. This study compared freeze-dried whole egg white (EWP), the gastrointestinal digestate of EWP (EWPD), fermented EWP, and fermented digestate in an oleic acid/palmitic acid-induced HepG2 lipid-accumulation model. Treatment doses normalized to the same amount of original EWP. Lipid accumulation and biochemical responses were evaluated, followed by reverse transcription–quantitative polymerase chain reaction, western blotting, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses.

RESULTS

EWP and its processed derivatives reduced intracellular triglyceride and total cholesterol levels and attenuated lipid-droplet accumulation to varying degrees. EWPD produced the largest numerical reduction in triglyceride content (30.94% vs. the model group). EWPD was associated with reduced expression of lipogenesis-related regulators, including sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c, fatty acid synthase, and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), together with changes in selected markers associated with lipid utilization and catabolic processes. Integrated omics analyses identified coordinated alterations in fatty acid biosynthesis, lipid transport, phospholipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism, and PPAR- and AMP-activated protein kinase-related annotations.

CONCLUSION

Overall, the EWPD showed greater cellular activity than intact EWP on an equal original-EWP-equivalent basis. These findings support the lipid-regulatory potential of EWP and its preparations in HepG2 cells, but further in vivo validation is needed. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
